criteria.evidence: T3 note (commit cb36162) states: "The outbox insert is committed in ClickEventRecorder's own @Transactional write transaction on the request thread before the 302 is written; UrlReadService (not in allowed files) keeps its read-only lookup transaction." The AC requires the outbox row to be committed in the SAME database transaction as the redirect handling; src/main/java/com/example/shortener/analytics/recording/ClickEventRecorder.java uses an independent write transaction, so the transactional-outbox atomicity guarantee is not met (a committed click can survive a failed/aborted redirect and vice versa). Field-level content (short_code, occurred_at, hashed_ip, referrer_host, idempotency key) is covered by ClickEventRecorderTest and RedirectClickRecordingIT, but the transaction-scope clause is not.

src/test/java/com/example/shortener/redirect/RedirectClickRecordingTest.java and RedirectClickRecordingIT.java; T3 note: "404/410 never reach the recorder"; recorder invocation sits in RedirectController.java only on the success branch.

src/test/java/com/example/shortener/analytics/it/KafkaUnavailableRedirectIT.java (redirect keeps status + Location with broker down, row stays PENDING); T3 note: "No Kafka or network I/O on the redirect path"; publishing is done off-thread by OutboxPoller on analyticsTaskScheduler (OutboxSchedulingConfig.java).

concerns: AC-1 atomicity deviation (blocking): the click row is written in ClickEventRecorder's own @Transactional boundary, not in the redirect handling transaction. This is a design change from the spec's transactional-outbox guarantee and was self-declared in the T3 note rather than raised as an ambiguity. Either the redirect path must join a single transaction, or the deviation needs an explicit ADR/spec amendment describing the accepted failure window (click recorded for a redirect that subsequently errors, or lost click if the commit fails after the lookup).

Security/authorization gap: T7 reports the codebase has no /api/v1 auth scheme, so GET /api/v1/urls/{short_code}/stats is served unauthenticated and per-link click volume for any guessable short code is publicly readable. AC-8 assumes an existing scheme exists; the plan DoD also required a 401 response in openapi.yaml and an unauthenticated test, neither of which was delivered. This is an unresolved ambiguity, not a safe default — escalate before release.

Retention scope risk: plan T6 risk_notes explicitly required the purge to exclude rows still awaiting publication, but the notes/data-model slice describe deleting click_outbox where occurred_at < now - retention.days with no status filter. If a row has been PENDING/FAILED for >90 days it is silently deleted (data loss, and FAILED rows lose their forensic trail). Confirm ClickRetentionJob filters on OutboxStatus and add a test for a 91-day-old PENDING row.

Verification gaps: T4, T6, T7 and T8 all report that `-Pit verify` was not executed (T1 too, "needs Docker"). The end-to-end IT, KafkaUnavailableRedirectIT, RedirectLatencyBudgetIT and the OpenAPI contract dump comparison are therefore unproven on the final tree. At minimum one clean `./mvnw -Pit verify` run on the merged branch should be evidenced before merge.

Latency gate credibility: the baseline is a committed static file (src/test/resources/analytics/redirect-latency-baseline.properties). Document how/when it was measured and ensure the IT uses warmup and a fixed sample size as the plan required, otherwise AC-13 is self-certifying.

PII gate handling in T8: the compliance finding was resolved by "rewording the README privacy bullet so it no longer spells the forbidden term". That is a scanner workaround, not a substantive fix. Confirm the scanner hit was genuinely a false positive in prose and that no code path logs or persists a client IP (spot-check ClickEventRecorder/RedirectController logging and any exception messages).

Secret handling: T1 notes a "non-secret local fallback" for SHORTENER_ANALYTICS_IP_SALT in application.yml. A defaulted salt that silently applies in a non-local profile would weaken every hashed_ip. Recommend fail-fast validation (@NotBlank plus a profile guard) so a missing salt aborts startup outside local/test.

Layering workaround: AnalyticsProperties is registered via a nested @Configuration because the application class was outside allowed_files (T1 note). Works, but leaves configuration wiring in an unusual place; flag for follow-up cleanup rather than leaving as precedent.

Observability: OutboxMetrics/ConsumerMetrics are hand-rolled because micrometer-core is absent. AC-5 asks for metered terminal failures; counters that are not exported to the platform's metrics backend give operators no alerting path. Confirm with the platform owner whether an in-memory counter satisfies the operator story (US-5).

No dead-letter/replay path: on retry exhaustion the consumer acks the record and marks EXHAUSTED, and the publisher marks the row FAILED and never retries. This matches AC-5's letter, but there is no documented operational procedure to replay FAILED/EXHAUSTED events; README/docs should state that these clicks are permanently lost.

Minor file-scope deviation: src/test/java/com/example/shortener/it/OpenApiContractIT.java was added under T7 whose allowed_files were src/test/java/**/analytics/api/**/*.java and src/main/resources/openapi.yaml. Harmless content-wise, but it sits outside the task's declared globs; record it or move it under the analytics package.

Lingering advisory failure: spotless:check has failed on src/test/java/com/example/shortener/analytics/aggregation/ClickStatsAggregatorTest.java since T5 and was deferred by T6, T7 and T8 as "outside allowed files". Since T5 authored it, it should be fixed rather than carried forward.

Migration numbering: V2__click_analytics.sql is the only migration added; confirm no collision with an existing V2 in the brownfield baseline (ClickAnalyticsMigrationTest should assert the full migration history applies from a clean schema, not just the new tables).
